DP 2.title: Climbing Stairs
DP 2.intuition: At any stair i, you can only arrive from stair (i-1) taking a 1-step, or from stair (i-2) taking a 2-step. Hence, the total number of distinct ways to reach stair i is ways(i) = ways(i-1) + ways(i-2). This directly mirrors the Fibonacci sequence.

ladder.explanation: Express problem in subproblems. f(n) = f(n-1) + f(n-2). Base cases: f(0)=1, f(1)=1. For n=45, 2^45 = 3.5e13 operations, which results in TLE.

ladder.complexity: O(N) Time, O(N) Space (Memo array + Stack)
ladder.explanation: Store results of subproblems in an array memo[] of size n+1 initialized to -1. If memo[n] != -1, return it directly.
Create dp array of size n+1. dp[0] = 1, dp[1] = 1. Loop from i = 2 to n: dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]. Return dp[n].
Notice dp[i] only needs the previous two states: prev1 = dp[i-1] and prev2 = dp[i-2]. We can maintain two variables and update prev2, prev1 = prev1, prev1 + prev2.

DP 3.title: Frog Jump
DP 3.intuition: The frog starts at index 0 and wants to reach index n-1. From stair i, it can jump to i+1 (cost |heights[i] - heights[i-1]|) or i+2 (cost |heights[i] - heights[i-2]|). To minimize total cost, at each step choose min(jumpOne, jumpTwo).

ladder.explanation: Cache intermediate jump results in dp table of size N.
Iterate from 1 to N-1, updating dp[i] from dp[i-1] and dp[i-2].
Only need prev1 and prev2 to store energy of previous two stairs.

code.python:
def frog_jump(heights: list) -> int:
    n = len(heights)
    if n <= 1:
        return 0
    prev2, prev1 = 0, abs(heights[1] - heights[0])
    for i in range(2, n):
        jump1 = prev1 + abs(heights[i] - heights[i - 1])
        jump2 = prev2 + abs(heights[i] - heights[i - 2])
        cur = min(jump1, jump2)
        prev2, prev1 = prev1, cur
    return prev1

DP 8.title: Grid Unique Paths
DP 8.intuition: In an m x n grid, to reach (i, j), you can only come from top (i-1, j) or left (i, j-1). Total paths to (i, j) is the sum of paths from (i-1, j) and (i, j-1).

ladder.explanation: dp[m][n] memo table saves redundant paths.
Bottom up: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1].
Notice we only need previous row values: prev_row[j] and current row running sum.

DP 19.title: 0/1 Knapsack
DP 19.intuition: For each item i with weight w and value v, you have two choices: leave it (dp[i-1][cap]) or take it if weight fits (dp[i-1][cap - w] + v). Take the maximum of both choices.

ladder.explanation: f(idx, cap) = max(f(idx-1, cap), val[idx] + f(idx-1, cap-wt[idx])).
dp[N][Capacity+1] matrix storing max value.
Iterate through items and capacities bottom-up.
Iterate capacity backwards from Cap down to wt[i] to compute 1D array in-place.

DP 25.title: Longest Common Subsequence
DP 25.intuition: Compare characters a[i-1] and b[j-1]. If they match, length is 1 + LCS(i-1, j-1). If they differ, best is max(LCS(i-1, j), LCS(i, j-1)).

ladder.explanation: f(i, j) = 1 + f(i-1, j-1) if match else max(f(i-1, j), f(i, j-1)).
2D table dp[m+1][n+1] storing LCS lengths.
Fill rows 1..m and cols 1..n.
Only need previous row array and current row array.
